draft.title: Sentence structures for effect
card: Writers shape sentences to create an effect on the reader. The length and pattern of a sentence are choices.
Periodic sentence

a long build-up that saves the main point for the end. It creates suspense, so the final words land with force. Example: After the storm, the blackout and three nights of waiting, the creek finally broke its banks.
Parallel structure
repeating the same pattern in a sentence. It creates balance and rhythm. Example: She came to learn, she came to lead, she came to win.
Short sentence
a very short sentence after longer ones draws attention to a point. Example: The door was open.
draft.remember: Sentence shape is a choice: build-up delays the point, parallel patterns balance it.

a.q: Which sentence saves its main point for the end to build suspense?
opts: After weeks of doubt and silence, the letter arrived
The letter arrived after weeks of doubt and silence
The letter came, and it was read, and it was kept
Letters arrive, letters are read, letters are kept
a.why: The first sentence holds back the main point, that the letter arrived, until the last words. In the second, the main point comes first, so there is no build-up. The last two use repeated patterns, which is a different effect.
a.clue: Where do the main words, the letter arrived, sit in each sentence?

b.q: Dev writes: We fixed the fence, we cleared the paddock, we saved the farm. What effect does the repeated pattern mainly create?
opts: Balance and rhythm that make the steps feel steady
Suspense, as the main point is held back to the end
Sudden emphasis, as one short sentence stands alone
Confusion, as the ideas are not linked in any way
b.why: Each part follows the same pattern, which is parallel structure, giving balance and rhythm. It is tempting to call it suspense because the last part is the biggest, but the main point is not delayed. It is one sentence, not a short sentence standing alone.
b.clue: Look at how each part of the sentence is built the same way.

a.best: After weeks of doubt and silence, the letter arrived

b.best: Balance and rhythm that make the steps feel steady

problems.detail: Why (a) names options by position ('the first sentence', 'the second', 'the last two'), but the options are shown in random order. As shown, the first option is a parallel sentence, so the explanation would point students to the wrong sentences. Refer to each option by its words instead.
